The three turbine blades analyzed are the C3X vane, the VKI rotor, and the ACE rotor.
Typical gas turbine film cooling situations involve steep polynomial profiles with their maxima shifted in upstream or downstream direction from the jet centerline.
The effect of coolant distribution at the hole exit can be as much as 60% on the heat transfer coefficient at the blade suction surface, and 50% at the pressure surface.
Different effects are observed on the pressure and suction surface depending upon the blade as well as upon the hole shape, conical or cylindrical.
The algebraic mixing length turbulence model of Baldwin and Lomax was used, along with Mayle's transition criterion and Forest's and Crawford's models for augmentation of heat transfer.
The incoming flow in the experimental tests on the ACE rotor had a turbulence intensity of 4.0 percent.

For the C3X vane, the heat transfer coefficient for each radial cooling hole was calculated from the measured coolant flow rate, coolant temperature, and a correction for thermal entry region effects.
For the VKI rotor, the local wall convective heat flux was deduced from the corresponding time-dependent surface temperature evolution provided by platinum thin-film gages.
For the ACE rotor, thin film platinum resistance thermometers were used to measure the heat transfer.
The grid size used for the C3X vane was 281 x 45 x 81, for the VKI rotor was 353 x 53 x 17, and for the ACE rotor was 313 x 53 x 17.
The code requires about 60 million words of storage and takes about 20 seconds per iteration (full-multigrid) on the C-90 machine for one million grid points.
The first case requires about 1100 iterations to converge, while subsequent cases for the same grid require about 300 iterations starting with the solution for the previous case.
The computational span is different from the real span for the blades to accommodate all the rows of holes.
The ratio of two adjacent grid sizes in any direction was kept within 0.76 to 1.3 for computational accuracy.
Periodic boundary conditions were used for the C3X vane and VKI rotor due to showerhead injection, while symmetry conditions were used for the ACE rotor.
